{{Short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=January 2025}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |year = 2024–25 |team = Wake Forest Demon Deacons |sport = Basketball |image = Wake Forest University Athletic logo.svg |image_size = |conference = Atlantic Coast Conference |division = |short_conf = ACC |CoachRank = |APRank = |record = 21–11 |conf_record = 13–7 |head_coach = [[Steve Forbes (basketball)|Steve Forbes]] |hc_year = 5th |asst_coach1 = [[BJ McKie]] |asst_coach2 = Matt Woodley |asst_coach3 = [[Jason Shay]] |asst_coach4 = [[Antanas Kavaliauskas]] |stadium = [[Lawrence Joel Veterans Memorial Coliseum|LJVM Coliseum]] |tourney = |tourney_result = }} {{2024–25 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2024–25 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team''' represented [[Wake Forest University]] during the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Demon Deacons, led by fifth-year head coach [[Steve Forbes (basketball)|Steve Forbes]], played their home games at the [[Lawrence Joel Veterans Memorial Coliseum]] in [[Winston-Salem, North Carolina]] as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. The Demon Deacons won their first four games of the season, the highlight of which, was a 72–70 victory over [[2024–25 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] at a neutral site. Their first loss came in the [[Skip Prosser]] Classic against [[2024–25 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]], 75–60. They won two games before traveling to [[Kissimmee, Florida|Florida]] to participate in the [[ESPN Events Invitational]]. The team lost to eighteenth ranked [[2024–25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the semifinals before defeating [[2024–25 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]] to finish in third place. They then traveled to [[College Station, Texas|College Station]] to face twenty-second ranked [[2024–25 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] in the [[ACC–SEC Challenge]], where they lost 57–44. The Demon Deacons won eight of their next nine games, with the only loss coming at twenty-fifth ranked [[2024–25 Clemson Tigers men's basketball team|Clemson]]. The run also included seven ACC wins, with a [[NC State–Wake Forest rivalry|rivalry]] victory over [[2024–25 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] and another [[North Carolina–Wake Forest rivalry|rivalry]] defeat of [[2024–25 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. The streak ended with back-to-back losses against ranked teams: second-ranked [[2024–25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] and twenty-first ranked [[2024–25 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]]. They won their next three games, including a two-point victory over [[2024–25 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]] and two victories on a trip to California. They lost 72–70 against [[2024–25 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] on their return to the east coast. The Demon Deacons went 3–3 in their final six games with defeats of [[2024–25 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]], [[2024–25 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]], and [[2024–25 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team|Georgia Tech]]. Their defeats over the stretch included a rivalry loss to NC State, a loss to [[2024–25 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|Virginia]], and another loss against second-ranked Duke. The Demon Deacons finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|season]] 21–11 and 13–7 in [[2024–25 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for fourth place. Wake Forest finished atop the tiebreaking procedure and was the fourth seed in the [[2025 ACC men's basketball tournament|2025 ACC tournament]]. As the fourth seed, they earned a bye into the quarterfinals where they lost to rivals North Carolina 68–59. They were not invited to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and declined an invitation to the [[2025 National Invitation Tournament|NIT]].{{cite web|url=https://www.wfmynews2.com/article/sports/basketball/wake-forest-mens-basketball-declines-nit-bid-season-over-2025/83-37214f01-e73c-47df-9176-fa4c95071c54|title=Wake Forest men's basketball declines NIT bid Season ends for Demon Deacons|work=[[WFMY-TV]]|first=Jeremy|last=Vernon|date=March 17, 2025|access-date=April 29, 2025}} ==Previous season== {{main|2023–24 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team}} The Demon Deacons finished the season 21–14 overall and 11–9 in [[2023–24 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for fifth place. After winning both tiebreakers, they were awarded the fifth seed in the [[2024 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]]. They received a bye into the second round where they defeated twelfth seed [[2023–24 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]], avenging a loss from the regular season. They lost to fourth seed [[2023–24 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|Pittsburgh]] in the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2024 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] and were a first seed. They defeated [[2023–24 Appalachian State Mountaineers men's basketball team|Appalachian State]] in the first round before losing to fourth-seed Georgia in the second round to end their season.
